question.text: Sahyadri Stat-Arb Fund, a Cat III AIF, wants to add a commodity-futures sleeve to its playbook. Per Section 2.6.1 (citing SEBI Circulars dated June 21, 2017 and September 29, 2017), what is the MAXIMUM percentage of investable funds a Cat III AIF may commit to ONE underlying commodity on the commodity-derivatives exchanges?

answer.text: There is no cap — Cat III is free to concentrate in a single commodity

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 2.6.1 states: 'Indian Category III AIFs are permitted by SEBI to invest in all commodity derivatives products that are being traded on the commodity derivatives exchanges. They can invest up to 10 percent of the investable funds in one underlying commodity, subject to the reporting requirements set forth by SEBI' (SEBI Circulars of 21-Jun-2017 and 29-Sep-2017). So the single-commodity cap is 10%. **The Trap:** Option A (5%) undershoots. Option C (25%) confuses with the close-ended single-investee concentration cap. Option D is the free-leverage myth — even Cat III has prudential concentration caps. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C (All-Cat Manager) carries the same circular reference. XIX-D (Cat I/II Manager) does NOT cover commodity-derivatives participation — Cat I/II do not invest in commodity derivatives this way. VIII (Equity Derivatives) covers the mechanics of the futures contracts themselves. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Pair this 10% single-commodity cap with the fund's overall 10% (open-ended) / 25% (close-ended) single-investee concentration limit. Reporting to SEBI on commodity exposures is separate from the monthly AIF returns — build the data pipeline once, and automate both feeds to avoid circular breaches.
